svg.title: From central triviality to one modular time
svg.desc: Four proved steps: a factorial corner gives a scalar phase; summable strong-star unitary corrections split off two Powers factors; their periods yield one common time; a slice of a tensor implementer makes the remaining automorphism inner times that time.

g.text: Central triviality determines a modular time
M: separable AFD III₁ factor · α ∈ Cnt(M) · λ, μ ∈ (0,1) · log λ / log μ irrational
1. A scalar phase in the asymptotic centralizer
E = [e₁₁], U = [α(e₁₂)e₂₁], U ∈ Z(EMωE) ⇒ U = γE, |γ| = 1
Mω is a II₁ factor; opposite weights make the displayed product centralizing.
Proof: CTM-01–02. Weighted factors preserve the strong* null errors in these products.
2. An exact split after one convergent inner correction
Ad(V) α = σ_t^ρ ⊗ β on P ⊗ Pᶜ, P ≅ Rλ, Pᶜ ≅ M
Vₙ = uₙVₙ₋₁ → V strongly*. Control both the fixed and conjugated state norms.
Proof: CTM-03. Infinitely many unselected matrix legs retain the required complement.
3. Two times have a common representative modulo their periods
Lλ = 2π / log λ, Lμ = 2π / log μ, t₁ − t₂ = rLλ + mLμ
T = t₁ − rLλ = t₂ + mLμ (r, m ∈ ℤ)
The actions agree with time T. The original numbers t₁ and t₂ need not agree.
Proof: CTM-04–06. Nonvanishing homogeneous partial isometries detect failure.
4. Flip, commute modulo inner automorphisms, then slice
(δβ⁻¹) ⊗ (βδ⁻¹) inner ⇒ δβ⁻¹ inner, δ = σ_T^ρ
Therefore α = Ad(u) σ_T^φ for a prescribed faithful normal state φ.
Proof: CTM-06–07. A nonzero slice v satisfies vx = a(x)v; factoriality normalizes v to a unitary.
Takesaki III, XVIII.4.29(ii), 4.32–4.33 · Complete argument accompanies this schematic · Original SVG: CC0
